FC01 ACLR — Adjacent Channel Leakage Ratio Advanced click to expand +

3GPP §6.6.2 · test_Tx_ACLR · Cadence P0/P1/P2 · ETM 1.1 · frequency fm

Plain English First
Your PA amplifies the wanted signal but also creates distortion products that leak into neighboring channels. ACLR measures how much power you're spilling on your neighbors. Higher dB = less leakage = better. 3GPP minimum is 45 dB. PW internal target for Metro/FHGW is 55 dB.
Pass/Fail Limits
HardwareLimitToleranceBand Override
COMBA OPT7.2 / OPT8≥ 45 dB±0.8 dBNone
FHGW Box / Metro≥ 55 dB±0.8 dBb0407, b0307_2nd_run, b082028_2nd_run, b41_1st_run → 52 dB
MiniMetro≥ 55 dB±1 dBNone
How Test Runs
ETM: 1.1 only (QPSK 1/3 — cleanest signal, easiest for PA) · Frequency: fm (band middle) · EXA measurement: ACP mode → 4 offsets (A_lo, A_up, B_lo, B_up) → worst case is verdict
Note: B-offset (±2×BW) often hits instrument noise floor → use A-offset (±BW) for real verdict
What If It Fails
DPD not converged → check DPD alignment in PreChecks · PA compression → output power too high, reduce gain · DAC clipping → CFR input power wrong register (0x534020004) · Cable VSWR → reflection re-enters PA, creates mixing products
Interview Q
Q: ACLR is 50 dB but spec is 45 dB — why might it still fail? A: FHGW Box and Metro have a tighter internal spec of 55 dB. The 3GPP 45 dB limit is the regulatory minimum; PW adds 10 dB margin for interference management.
Real RCT Implementation — actual code from the test framework
Files: measure_test_Tx_ACLR (features/tech_4g/conformance_unified_lte_tx_speed.py) · analyzer setup config_te_for_lte_acp (infrastructure/utils.py) · fetch sa_acp_acquire_averaged (test_equipment/te_equipments.py).# config_te_for_lte_acp (utils.py) INST:SEL LTEAFDD CONF:ACPower MMEMory:LOAD:MASK ".../ACP_BS/ACP_BS_{bw}MHz_pairE-UTRA_CatB.mask" :SENSe:ACPower:OFFSet:LIST:STATe ON,ON,OFF,OFF,OFF # A(+/-BW) + B(+/-2xBW) :SENSe:ACPower:AVERage:COUNt 10 :SENSe:ACPower:AVERage:STATe ON # sa_acp_acquire_averaged (te_equipments.py) :INIT:ACP ; verify_opc() ; FETCh:ACPower10? # -> ~40-value tableResult parse: ACLR_CHANNEL_IDX = (3,13,23,33) → abs() of A_lower, A_upper, B_lower, B_upper.
KPI (Metro_kpi_thresholds.json): test_Tx_ACLR.min_limit = 55 dBc, tolerance = 0. limits_validation_aclr (utils.py): each offset PASS if meas > limit (higher = better).
Band override (the 52 dBc): the validator reads band_min_limit["{fhgw_band}_{dualband_step}"] → 52 dBc for the 2nd-run / dual-band cases (b0307_second_run, b0407, b082028_second_run, b41_first_run).
Quirks: 10-sweep ACP averaging (GRDEV-8508, ~0.2 dB margin on B7 top channel); the B offset (±2×BW) often sits at the instrument noise floor, so the A offset is the real verdict.
Real RCT quirk — auto-range (min-clip) before ACLR (PR 586 / GRDEV-8131)
measure_test_Tx_ACLR was the only TX measure missing the analyzer auto-range that every other TX test already did. Added before the ACP read:ant.equiphandler.sa_set_atten_for_min_clipping() # SENSe:POWer:RF:RANGe:OPTimize IMMediate"Min-clip" = adjust the analyzer input range for max dynamic range without overload. Without it, the per-RFFE isolated (lower-power) signal read ACLR near the noise floor → degraded 51–52 dBc; with it each isolated path auto-ranges → 54.5–55.6 dBc (+2–3 dB). EVM always passed because its measure already auto-ranged. (See FC20 for per-RFFE IQ playback.)

3GPP §6.6.2 · test_Tx_ACLR · framework: ruauto · concrete setup: RCT-4G-GR-AAU-B1B3-TRX7 · paths are repo-relative to ruauto/source/ unless noted · this is the "how the automation actually does it" companion to the ACLR card above

The whole flow in one line
A priority profile (P0/P1/P2…) names test groups → groups list Test-IDs → test_Tx_ACLR registration declares freqs/ETMs & report columns → the road-trip loop sets the DUT transmitting an E-TM and dispatches measure_test_Tx_ACLR by name → it drives the analyzer in ACP mode, fetches 4 adjacent-channel ratios → limits_validation_aclr compares each to the KPI limit → verdicts written to Excel + CI/Elastic.
① What configuration the test needs
Four files in the setup folder drive ACLR. The runner is fully config-driven — no test code changes per setup.

tc_cadence.jsonTest-ID test_Tx_ACLR: {frequency:["fm"], etm:["1.1","1.2"]} · it's in groups TS_DL_CI / Nightly / Regression / Sanity · priorities P0,P1,P2,P3 (via the DL groups; not P4/P5)
fdd_test_setup.jsonbands ["1","3"], BSClass:"Wide" · antenna_mapping socket 5025 rfio1–4 · DLFreqs [1720,1750,1770] · path_loss "-10" · Tx.Power.b0103
env_setup.jsonthe active analyzer (use_for_test:true) = Keysight EXF E6550A @ 10.196.60.12:5025 · cable-loss per socket/freq in cable_loss.json
Metro_kpi_thresholds.json
(via setup.ini → ../kpi_thresholds_references/)		the pass limit: test_Tx_ACLR: {min_limit:55, tolerance:0, "3gpp_reference":"6.6.2"} → ≥ 55 dB flat for this setup (FHGW_Box file adds tolerance 0.8 + per-band overrides to 52)
ETM waveform: not a file loaded to the analyzer — the E-TM 1.1/1.2 signal is PHY-generated on the DUT by the testmac command rctdl <test_num> <bw> over SSH. The analyzer only loads an ACP limit mask ACP_BS_{bw}MHz_pairE-UTRA_CatB.mask.

④ How results are captured
The ACP table has ~40 slots; ACLR reads 4 fixed indices (the two A offsets at ±BW and two B offsets at ±2×BW), all made positive with abs().
ACLR_CHANNEL_IDX = (3, 13, 23, 33)     # L3076  A_Lower, A_Upper, B_Lower, B_Upper
measured = [abs(float(table[i])) for i in ACLR_CHANNEL_IDX]   # L3168
A_lo, A_up, B_lo, B_up = measured
result = LteUtils.limits_validation_aclr(measured)            # L3170  -> verdicts (see ⑤)
# marginal fail within 1.0 dB of limit -> _remeasure_aclr_if_marginal (L3081-3107, uses mean)
Written to: Excel sheet test_Tx_ACLR via xlxfile.write_result(..., one_line=True) (L3219) — all 4 values, each with its Verdict + pass/min criteria columns · CI/Elastic via tc.update_new_elastic(...) (L3220) · running verdict via verdict += [r0,r1,r2,r3] (L3221) → commit_running_verdict · analyzer screenshots to ScreenShots_ACLR_Band{n}_{ant}/.
⑤ How pass/fail is decided
One function: LteUtils.limits_validation_aclr() in infrastructure/utils.py (L4956-5012). Higher ACLR is better, so the test fails when a measured ratio is ≤ the limit.
# threshold resolution order (first hit wins):
#  1) kpi_thresholds["test_Tx_ACLR"].min_limit + .tolerance   (+ band overrides)
#  2) tc_cadence["aclr_min_limit"], tolerance = 0.8
#  3) hard fallback: min_limit = 45, tolerance = 0.8   ("3GPP standard")
# -> this setup hits (1): min_limit = 55, tolerance = 0

aclr_pass_limit = aclr_min_limit - tolerance          # 55 - 0 = 55
for meas in measured:                                 # all 4 offsets, independently
    min_result  = FAIL if meas <= aclr_min_limit  else PASS
    pass_result = FAIL if meas <= aclr_pass_limit else PASS
return pass_results, aclr_pass_limit, min_results, aclr_min_limit
Key point: all four offsets are judged independently — the run fails if any one offset fails. There is no single "worst-case" number reduced before comparison; each ratio must be strictly > the limit. For this setup both the "min" and "pass" lines sit at 55 dB (tolerance 0).
Consolidated pseudo-code (copy/paste memory aid)
run_aclr(setup, priority=P0):
    cfg   = load(setup/tc_cadence.json)
    kpi   = load(setup/setup.ini -> kpi_thresholds_references/Metro_kpi_thresholds.json)
    equip = load(setup/env_setup.json).analyzer where use_for_test   # EXF E6550A :5025
    hw    = load(setup/fdd_test_setup.json)                          # bands, power, path_loss, sockets

    groups   = cfg.Cadence-IDs[priority]          # P0 -> [TS_DL_CI, TS_UL_CI]
    testlist = flatten(cfg.Group-IDs[g].Tests for g in groups)
    if "test_Tx_ACLR" not in testlist: return
    etms  = cfg.Test-IDs.test_Tx_ACLR.etm         # ["1.1","1.2"]
    freqs = cfg.Test-IDs.test_Tx_ACLR.frequency   # ["fm"]
    limit = kpi.test_Tx_ACLR.min_limit            # 55  (tolerance 0)

    for band in hw.bands:                         # 1, 3
      for bw in group.BW[band]:                   # e.g. 10
        for etm in etms:                          # 1.1, 1.2
          for f in resolve(freqs, band, bw):      # fm -> actual MHz
            DUT.rctdl(testnum(bw,etm), bw)        # PHY emits E-TM  (SSH)
            wait_active_transmission()
            analyzer.config_acp(f, bw)            # LTEAFDD, CONF:ACP, load mask, avg=10
            table = analyzer.acp_acquire_averaged()      # INIT:ACP; FETC:ACPower10?
            offs  = [abs(table[i]) for i in (3,13,23,33)]# A_lo,A_up,B_lo,B_up
            verdict = [ "PASS" if x > limit else "FAIL" for x in offs ]
            xlsx.write("test_Tx_ACLR", f, bw, etm, offs, verdict, limit)
            CI.push(offs, verdict)
    # overall ACLR = PASS iff every offset of every (band,bw,etm,freq) is PASS

3GPP §6.2 / §6.5 · test_Tx_modulation_analysis · ONE EXA modulation-analysis session → 5 metrics · file features/tech_4g/conformance_unified_lte_tx_speed.py · setup RCT-4G-GR-AAU-B1B3-TRX7

Why it's a composite
Reading a full LTE demod frame on the analyzer is slow, so the framework reads the Frame Summary table once per antenna and pulls all five TX-quality metrics from that single read. test_Tx_modulation_analysis has no freq/etm of its own (tc_cadence L17-18 is just a _note); each sub-test keeps its own Test-ID entry, and a group-level etm can override via the group_via trick (utils get_tc_cadence_param L115).

FC02 EVM — Error Vector Magnitude Advanced click to expand +

3GPP §6.5.2 · test_Tx_EVM · Cadence P1 (via modulation_analysis) · ETM-dependent

Plain English First
EVM measures how far each IQ symbol lands from its ideal position on the constellation. Think of it as aiming accuracy — 0% is perfect, higher % = more scatter. 64QAM needs tighter clustering (≤3.5%) than QPSK (≤17.5%). Anything above limit = blocks decoded incorrectly.
EVM% Formula
EVM% = √(Σ|error_vector|² / Σ|ideal_vector|²) × 100
Error vector = difference between actual measured IQ point and ideal IQ point
Limits by ETM
ETM CodeModulation3GPP LimitMetro/FHGW InternalTest Use
1.1QPSK 1/3, 6 RBs≤ 17.5%≤ 3.5%Standard nightly
2aQPSK+64QAM mix≤ 3.5%≤ 3.5%Regression
3.164QAM full BW≤ 8.0%≤ 3.5%Regression
3.1a64QAM alternate≤ 3.5%≤ 3.5%Regression
3.216QAM≤ 12.5%—Regression
3.3QPSK full BW≤ 17.5%—Regression
What If It Fails
IQ imbalance → constellation rotated/skewed → check IQ calibration registers · LO phase noise → symbol cloud diffuse → check PLL lock · DAC nonlinearity → even/odd harmonics → reduce DAC input level · DPD failure → PA distortion uncorrected → check DPD alignment status · Temperature → EVM degrades above 55°C PA junction temp
Interview Q
Q: ETM 1.1 limit is 17.5% but you're testing at 3.5% — why? A: 3GPP 17.5% is the regulatory floor. Metro internal spec is 3.5% for all ETMs — if we pass 3.5% on ETM 1.1, we know the radio is well within margin for any operator requirement.
Real RCT Implementation — actual code from the test framework
Files: composite measure_test_Tx_modulation_analysis reads table['EVM'] from the frame-summary; standalone measure_test_Tx_EVM uses a dedicated CEVM fetch.# standalone EVM (te_equipments.py) CONF:CEVM sa_evm_test_etm_vs_modulation(etm) # picks the right metric per ETM: 1.1 -> EVM ; 2a/3.1a -> 3GPP-256QAM EVM ; 3.1/2.0 -> 3GPP-64QAM EVM 3.2 -> 16QAM ; 3.3 -> QPSK FETCH:CEVM1? # standalone read # composite path CALC:EVM:DATA4:TABL:STR? # frame summary -> table['EVM'], table['EVMPeak']KPI: test_Tx_EVM.etm_dependent = true, every ETM min_limit = 3.5%, tolerance = 0. limits_validation_EVM (utils.py:4473): PASS if EVM ≤ 3.5% (lower = better). 3GPP floor is 8–17.5% by ETM — PW is far stricter.
EVM RMS vs Peak %
The frame-summary table carries two numbers: EVM (RMS, averaged over all subcarriers/symbols) and EVMPeak (the single worst RE). RMS is the pass metric (vs 3.5%); Peak is a diagnostic.
A high Peak/RMS ratio points to a sporadic impairment (one bad subcarrier, an LO spur, a DAC glitch) rather than uniform noise — if RMS is fine but Peak spikes, look for a localized defect, not a broadband SNR problem. Uniform thermal/quantization noise gives a low, steady Peak/RMS.
EVM Peak % vs RMS EVM — your early warning system
RMS EVM = root-mean-square over all symbols — the 3GPP/Metro pass metric (≤ 3.5%). EVM Peak = the worst single symbol, typically 3–5× RMS; not a BS limit, but the EXA reports it — use it for debug.
PatternMeaningLikely cause
Peak >> RMS (e.g. 2% / 15%)impulse distortion — occasional bad symbolsPA clipping on a PAPR spike, PLL phase hit, IQ-sample drop in eCPRI, B41 TDD trigger glitch
Peak ≈ RMS (e.g. 3% / 4%)uniform distortion — consistent impairmentIQ imbalance, LO leakage, DC offset, sustained phase noise, constant DPD error
Example: RMS 3.2% passes Metro's 3.5%, but Peak 14% reveals an intermittent fault — in the field it causes sporadic CRC failures + HARQ retransmits. Read both on the EXA: Modulation Analysis → Summary.
Q: EVM RMS 3.0% (passes) but Peak 18% — pass the test? Technically yes (spec is RMS-only), but 18% peak = one-in-N symbols severely wrong. Flag it and hunt the impulse source before sign-off: B41 TDD trigger timing, eCPRI sequence errors, the CFR register value.
Real RCT quirk — EVM modulation-table crash-guard (ECS)
table['EVM'] → table.get('EVM') (also ChannelPower, TimeOffset, FreqErr, RSTP). When the analyzer couldn't demod-sync, the modulation table came back missing those keys entirely → KeyError: 'EVM' hard-crashed the whole TX road-trip at the first frequency (seen on B8 real-tx). Now a no-sync read degrades to 0/fail (what the file's own _safe_float already intends) instead of crashing — the run completes and produces the full per-antenna/per-freq table. Behaviour is unchanged when the key is present.

3GPP §6.6.3 · test_lte_Tx_Mask · Regression cadence only

Plain English First
A mask drawn around your channel — your emissions must stay below it at every frequency offset. Think of it as the shape your signal is allowed to occupy. Anything leaking outside = FAIL. Unlike ACLR (which measures one adjacent channel), SEM checks the full spectrum shape.

Real RCT Implementation — actual code from the test framework
Files: measure_test_lte_Tx_Mask (conformance_unified_lte_tx_speed.py) → config_te_for_lte_mask (utils.py) → sa_load_mask_setup(get_sem_mask_setup_name(bw, dl_freqGHz, duplex)) → FETCh:SEMask10?. The analyzer loads a per-(bw, freq, duplex) mask file and returns pass/fail + worst margin per segment.Mask (Metro_kpi_thresholds.json → test_lte_Tx_Mask, array [Δf_start, Δf_stop, limit_start, limit_stop, MBW]):

> 10.5 MHz−151 MHz
3GPP §6.6.3. Note the KPI comment literally reads "Operating band unwanted emissions (SEM)" — so this test is the OBUE test (see FC18).
What SEM actually measures — the mask explained
The mask is a continuous power-limit envelope vs frequency offset from the CHANNEL EDGE (not from carrier centre). For a 20 MHz channel the edge sits at ±10 MHz from centre, so a "0–5 MHz offset" point is 10–15 MHz from the carrier.
Offset from edgeMeas BWRepresentative 3GPP limit
0–5 MHz30 kHz−10 dBm
5–10 MHz30 kHz−13 dBm
10–25 MHz30 kHz−25 dBm
> 25 MHz30 kHz−25 dBm
Note: the table above is the generic wide-area-BS shape. The actual mask your RCT loads is stricter and per-band — see the "Metro SEM Limits" box above (−14 dBm near-edge tapering to −26, then −13/−15 dBm), loaded as a per-(bw, freq, duplex) mask file by config_te_for_lte_mask.
SEM vs ACLR — what each catches
ACLR = integrated power in one adjacent-channel bandwidth → one number per neighbour; catches broadband spectral regrowth.
SEM = continuous spectral envelope → catches a narrow spur near the edge and asymmetric distortion. ACLR can PASS while SEM FAILS if a single narrow spur pokes above the mask just outside the channel. They are complementary — always run both.
Multi-band SEM — the B1+B3 interaction
With B1 (2140 MHz) and B3 (1842 MHz) both active, IM3 products appear:2*f_B1 - f_B3 = 4280 - 1842 = 2438 MHz (near B41 - can hit B41 SEM if B41 active) 2*f_B3 - f_B1 = 3684 - 2140 = 1544 MHz (in B1 UL - can hit B1 UL protection)This inter-band IMD is why the dual-band 2nd-run ACLR limit relaxes to 52 dBc (b0103) — SEM gets an equivalent relaxation. Debug: SEM fails only with the second carrier active → inter-band IMD, not a DPD problem (DPD linearises one carrier at a time). Check inter-band isolation between the PA output paths.
Worked example — B3 @ 1812.5 MHz / 15 MHz (Metro AAU, PNG customer)
Channel: 1812.5 ± 7.5 = 1805–1820 MHz (the wanted 52.5 dBm). DL operating band B3: 1805–1880 MHz (3GPP-fixed). SEM territory (§6.6.3): band edge ±10 MHz = 1795–1890 MHz — crucially measured from the band edges, not your channel. Because this 15 MHz sits at the very bottom of B3, the SEM region extends far above you (to 1890) but barely below (to 1795).Vendor mask actually loaded (bands >1 GHz, Cat B; TS 36.104 Table 6.6.3.2.1-6 — one table for 5/10/15/20 MHz, so the 10 and 15 MHz mask files are identical):
Offset from edgeLimitMeas BW
0.05–5.05 MHz−5.5 → −12.5 dBm (sloped)51 kHz
5.05–10.05 MHz−12.5 dBm100 kHz
10.5–15 MHz−15 dBm1 MHz
The failing 10.5–15 MHz segment lands at ~1830.5–1835 MHz — inside B3's band, so the limit legitimately applies. Measured −14.83 dBm vs −15, and it repeats across three antennas (A −14.83, C −14.09, D −15.44) → the single most credible genuine radio finding in the campaign. (RBW matters: the same emission in 51 kHz vs 1 MHz differs by 10·log₁₀(1e6/RBW) ≈ +12.9 dB — we log the raw value in its own RBW, because that's what the 3GPP limit is specified against.)
Frequency territories & why the framework splits spurious into 5
1795 1805 CHANNEL 1820 1880 1890 ──────┼──────────┼─────────────┼───────────────────────┼──────┼────► │ │ wanted │ │ │ │◄──────── DL operating band (1805-1880) ─────────►│ │ │◄──────────── SEM territory 6.6.3 (1795-1890) ───────────►│ spurious 6.6.4 ◄─┘ └─► spurious3GPP defines 4 spurious ranges; the framework splits the last (1 GHz–12.75 GHz) around the SEM gap — for B3 that gap is exactly 1.795–1.89 GHz — giving 5 rows, so SEM (§6.6.3) and spurious (§6.6.4) neither overlap nor double-count. The sweep stops at 12.75 GHz because 7 harmonics of 1812.5 MHz fit below it.
Why only 2nd/3rd harmonics matter: the PA transfer series coefficients collapse (a₁ ≫ a₂ ≫ a₃, ~20 dB/order), the top harmonic gets the smallest algebraic share (cos³ gives 3f only ¼; cos⁵ gives 5f only 1⁄16), and the post-PA low-pass filter attenuates more with distance — by the 4th harmonic you're below the noise floor.
Real failure from the field — BSNL B1 run (fhgw.log)
From ruauto's auto-collected fhgw.log (136k lines, B1 antenna-A run @ DL 2159/2164). The RU never attenuates: all 303 power-scale ops read Attenuation: 0 dB, gain 0x11cc — constant, unattenuated gain across every E-TM. So the dynamic-range (§6.4) 1.1–1.2 dB deficit (measured 15.66–15.82 vs 16.9 dB limit) is not the RU gain chain — it points at the E-TM 2 OSTP measurement (an unoccupied-subcarrier noise pedestal inflating the min-power figure) or DU baseband scaling. Confirming: the 15 MHz 2.0→3.1 pair even passes (20.17 vs 18.7), so it's not a fixed RU limit.
Also: the 38 unit-out-of-order alarms are benign (carriers torn down to reconfigure freq/E-TM); no DPD state is logged (would need on-device /run/media logs to judge ACLR 53–56 dBc vs the 55 target); and dac_current_values has no B1 entry (B3/B28/B41 do) — a real gap, but not the root cause since B3 also fails §6.4.
Real RCT gotcha — SEM segment mis-indexing (GRDEV-7734, Change 2)
The analyzer returns SEM as a flat list of (lower, upper) pairs — segment n lives at indices 2n / 2n+1. A defect used deltas_table_ind = 1 (never incremented), so segments 3, 4, 5 displayed a neighbouring segment's value and three genuine measurements (slots 7,8,9) were never read.- deltas_table_ind = 1 # never incremented -> wrong from segment 3 + lower_ind, upper_ind = 2*ind, 2*ind+1 # correct 2n / 2n+1 + if len(deltas_table) <= upper_ind: break # bounds guard, no IndexErrorVerified on the E6680A: :FETCh:SEMask15? returns 24 fields, 10 real at indices 0–9, the rest 9.91E+37 (Keysight "no result"). Verdicts did not change (SEM genuinely exceeds the mask by ~0.2–2.4 dB) — the fix corrects which segment each number is shown against, which is exactly what an RU-side investigation uses. Silent for ~12 months because the two live nightlies fall back to 3 segments (only the last wrong); ours was the first to run 5 segments and exposed 3 of 5.

FC09 Reference Sensitivity — Minimum RX Power Advanced click to expand +

3GPP §7.2 / TS 36.104 · test_Rx_Reference_Sensitivity_Level · Cadence P0/P1/P2

Plain English First
The weakest signal the RU can still decode correctly. EXM injects a signal at decreasing power until BLER hits 5% threshold. That power level = sensitivity. Lower number = more sensitive = better. Your B1 sensitivity is approximately −102 dBm theoretical (from NF chain calculation).
Pass/Fail Limits (FHGW Box)
Method: base_dbm + DSA(band) = runtime sensitivity_limit
base_dbm: −73 dBm (pre-DSA global KPI)

Band comboBandExpected sensitivity_limit
b0103B1−68 dBm
b0103B3−68 dBm
b082028B8−67 dBm
b082028B20−60 dBm
b082028B28−60 dBm
b41B41−66 dBm
3GPP Pass Condition
FRCBWBLER ThresholdA-level
A1-11.4 MHz−69 dBany
A1-35/10/15/20 MHz−69 dBany
Search Algorithm
Stage 1 Coarse: init_power=−63 dBm → step −1 dB (coarse_step=1)
Stage 2 Fine: fine_step=0.6 dB around crossing point
Stage 3 Finest: finest_step=0.2 dB final precision
Abort: bler_100_max_steps=1 → if BLER≥99% for 1 step, abort as FAIL (UL path dead)
DSA Runtime Adjustment
VruDsaMixin.apply_dsa_adjustments_from_ru() → SSH into RU → reads /etc/configs/personalities/<model>-rfdc.txt → DSA(band) per ADC → final KPI = base_dbm + DSA(band)
DSA column appears in Excel report for traceability
What If It Fails
RX path open/broken → BLER stays 100% at all powers → bler_100_max_steps triggers · DSA mismatch → sensitivity shifted by DSA error amount · LNA failed → NF jumps ~20 dB → sensitivity degrades severely · ADC_ADJUST wrong → RSSI reads wrong, sensitivity calc offset · Your unit #510 → B1C, B1D, B3D dead → exactly this scenario
Real RCT Implementation — actual code from the test framework
Files: configure_test_Rx_Reference_Sensitivity_Level (conformance_unified_lte_rx_speed.py) → rx_knee_seeded_search → Utils.find_sensitive_point (utils.py); BLER read via get_statistics_ts_fox (testmac "ts fox").# 3-stage descent to the 5% BLER knee (test_parameters, Metro json) init_power = -52 dBm ; fault_power = -51 (abort ceiling) coarse_step = 2.5 dB -> fine_step = 0.6 dB -> finest_step = 0.2 dB bler_threshold = 5 % (target BLER on FRC A1-3) # DSA / start power (products/rrh/fhgw.py) sens_point = -105 (RFFE) else -75 back_off_pwr = 5 start_pwr = int(sens_point + back_off_pwr - setup_loss)FHGW DSA runtime limit: kpi_limit = base_dbm + DSA(band), DSA read per-ADC from the RU rfdc.txt by apply_dsa_adjustments_from_ru() — so the sensitivity KPI tracks the actual front-end attenuation of each unit.
Effective pass limit (this setup): rx_limits_validation_conditions gives Wide-Area / A1-3 = −69 dBm, +0.7 dB tolerance → −68.3 dBm — this overrides the KPI base_dbm = −101.5.
Data vs PRACH sensitivity: data uses FRC A1-3 throughput/BLER descent (this card); PRACH uses preamble detection (miss ≤ 1%) — a different metric (FC10).

FC09D Sensitivity — Debug Playbook: isolating a low-sensitivity RU (from a real escalation) Debug click to expand +

3GPP §7.2 · TS 36.104 / 36.141 · "why is B28 RX sensitivity short?" — the step-by-step isolation an interviewer loves

The formula, and what each term means
PREFSENS = −174 + 10·log10(BW) + NF + IM + SNR  (dBm)
• −174 dBm/Hz = thermal noise floor (kTB at room temp).
• 10·log10(BW) = noise power over the occupied bandwidth (Hz).
• NF = BS noise figure — 3GPP: 5 dB Wide-Area, 10 dB Medium-Range, 13 dB Local-Area.
• IM = implementation margin = 2 dB.
• SNR = the SNR that reaches 95% throughput on the FRC (per-BW, from simulation; usually slightly negative).
Example (1.4 MHz): −174 + 10log10(1.1M) + 5 + 2 + (−0.6) ≈ −107.3 dBm.
3GPP BS reference sensitivity (single RX port, f ≤ 3 GHz)
BW (MHz)FRCTS 36.104TS 36.141 (f ≤ 3 GHz)
1.4A1-1−106.8−106.1
3A1-2−103.0−102.3
5 / 10 / 15 / 20A1-3−101.5−100.8
Note: for BW ≥ 5 MHz the requirement is met by applying FRC A1-3 to consecutive 25-RB chunks. Pass = throughput ≥ 95% at the reference level.
RX combining gain — the number people forget
The 3GPP number above is per single RX port. The product combines multiple RX branches, so the system-level sensitivity is better than the single-port figure by the combining gain:
• Mid band (B1/B3): 4-RX combining → ≈ +6 dB
• Low band incl. B28: 2-RX combining → ≈ +3 dB
So a single-port measurement of ~−104 to −105 dBm on B28 becomes ~−107 to −108 dBm after 2-RX combining. Always state which one you're quoting — comparing a single-port measurement against a combined requirement (or vice-versa) is the #1 cause of a "sensitivity looks short" false alarm. B28 has less combining headroom (3 dB) than mid-band (6 dB), so it's the first to look marginal.
The isolation sequence (run in this order)
1 · Pin the firmware. Record the FHGW FW version the shortfall was seen on, and re-measure on a second FW build — rules out a FW/calibration regression before you touch hardware.

2 · +5 dB ADC attenuation, then re-measure. This is the key discriminator:
  • sensitivity degrades with +5 dB → not enough system gain / RX gain margin → investigate the RX gain path (LNA, front-end, DSA/ADC_ADJUST).
  • sensitivity ≈ unchanged with +5 dB → the ADC input level isn't the limiter → look at the DU / UL demod / BLER measurement path (decode, not RF).

3 · Change the test frequency. Move to a different (clean) in-band frequency. If it recovers, you had external RF interference, not an RU fault — verify the frequency is clean first.

4 · Compare to a reference/certification measurement. Line it up against a known-good result, but normalise first: account for the combining gain (2-RX vs single port) and any difference in the cable-loss application method — don't chase an absolute-value gap that's just a measurement convention.
How the ADC-attenuation check looks at the CLI
get-atten-dfe <ant> <cc> <atten×10> sets the digital front-end ADC attenuation; then inject the FRC and read power-monitor (UL dBFS), get-rssi (dBFS/dBm) and BLER. Sweeping ADC-ATT shows the sensitivity level at the filter input vs the ADC headroom:
ADC ATTSG @ filter inputget-rssi (dBFS)BLER (%)
0 dB−107.8 dBm−55.91.5
10 dB−106.9 dBm−64.51.5
20 dB−102.4 dBm−65.21.3
27 dB−96.5 dBm−inf (not detected)1.2
More ADC attenuation eats RX headroom → the achievable sensitivity level rises (worsens). If adding attenuation barely moves BLER/sensitivity, the limit is downstream (DU/demod), not the ADC input.
Interview Q&A
Q: A B28 unit looks ~3 dB short on RX sensitivity — how do you debug it?
A: First check it isn't a measurement mismatch: the 3GPP number is per single RX port, but B28 uses 2-RX combining (~3 dB), so confirm I'm comparing like-for-like and normalise the cable-loss method. Then pin the FW version (re-test on a second build), add +5 dB ADC attenuation — if sensitivity degrades it's an RX-gain/system-gain problem (LNA/front-end/DSA), if it's unchanged the limit is in the DU/UL-demod/BLER path — and finally move to a clean frequency to rule out external interference.
Q: Why does mid-band have more sensitivity margin than B28?
A: Combining gain. Mid band (B1/B3) combines 4 RX branches (~6 dB), low band including B28 combines only 2 (~3 dB), so B28 has half the combining headroom and shows up marginal first.
Q: What does adding ADC attenuation tell you in a sensitivity investigation?
A: It separates an RF-gain limit from a decode limit. If +5 dB of ADC attenuation worsens sensitivity, the RX chain didn't have enough gain margin; if sensitivity barely moves, the ADC input level isn't the bottleneck and the problem is downstream in the DU/UL demodulation/BLER path.

FC17 OBW — Occupied Bandwidth (99% power) TX Conformance click to expand +
Why it exists
OBW is the bandwidth that contains 99% of the transmitted power. It confirms the signal isn't spreading wider than its channel — a first, cheap sanity check on spectral containment (ACLR/SEM then check the leakage outside it). 3GPP §6.6.1.
Real RCT Implementation — actual code from the test framework
Files: measure_test_Tx_Occupied_Bandwidth (conformance_unified_lte_tx_speed.py) → config_te_for_lte_obw (utils.py) → sa_set_OBW_mode (te_equipments.py).sa_set_OBW_mode() # -> CONF:OBWidth SENSe:OBWidth:FREQuency:SPAN {span} FETCh:OBWidth? # returns the 99%-power bandwidthKPI (Metro_kpi_thresholds.json → test_Tx_Occupied_Bandwidth): per BW min_limit = the channel BW itself (5→5, 10→10, 15→15, 20→20 MHz), tolerance = 0. PASS if OBW ≤ channel BW.
Interview Q&A
Q: OBW vs ACLR? OBW measures where 99% of your power sits (containment); ACLR measures how much leaks into the neighbour channel. A clean OBW can still fail ACLR if the last 1% tail is high.
OBW deep dive — formula, procedure, causes
Formula: integrate total TX power across the span, then OBW = f_upper(99.5%) − f_lower(0.5%) — the band holding the middle 99%. Typical clean LTE: ~18 MHz for a 20 MHz channel. Limit: OBW ≤ channel BW.EXA procedure: Mode LTE-FDD · Meas OBW · Span ≥ 3× channel BW · read the OBW result directly.
OBW too wide? DPD not converged (spectral regrowth), CFR over-clipping, or PA saturation — same root causes as failing ACLR/SEM.
vs SEM: OBW measures the wanted signal's width; SEM measures the unwanted emissions outside it.
Q: OBW reads 21.5 MHz on a 20 MHz channel — what's wrong? Spectral regrowth. Check DPD convergence first (ACLR is almost certainly also failing). Run dpd-app-orx --debug to see if DPD is tracking.
FC18 OBUE — Operating Band Unwanted Emissions TX Conformance click to expand +
Why it exists
OBUE (3GPP §6.6.3) bounds the unwanted emissions across (and just outside) the operating band with the spectrum emission mask. In this RCT framework OBUE and SEM are the same measurement — the KPI entry test_lte_Tx_Mask is literally commented "Operating band unwanted emissions (SEM)" (see FC07). This card frames it from the OBUE side.
Real RCT Implementation — actual code from the test framework
Same as FC07 (SEM): measure_test_lte_Tx_Mask → config_te_for_lte_mask → sa_load_mask_setup(get_sem_mask_setup_name(bw, dl_freqGHz, duplex)) → FETCh:SEMask10?. The mask ranges (see FC07 table: −14 dBm near-edge tapering to −26, then −13/−15 dBm flat) are the OBUE limits.
OBUE vs Spurious
OBUE covers the region from the channel edge out to the operating-band edge + Δf_OOB (mask-bounded, relative-ish). Beyond that it becomes Spurious emissions (FC19), which use absolute far-out limits (−36/−30 dBm). Same analyzer, different frequency regime and limit type.
Interview Q&A
Q: OBUE vs spurious emissions? OBUE is the near-carrier mask across the operating band (SEM); spurious is the far-out sweep (9 kHz–12.75 GHz) against fixed absolute limits.
OBUE in depth — in-band, outside your channel
Conceptually OBUE = emissions within the operating band but outside your assigned channel. Reconciliation: in 3GPP TS 36.141 (and this RCT framework) OBUE §6.6.3 IS the spectrum-emission-mask test — the same test_lte_Tx_Mask as FC07. The near-edge portion of that mask is exactly this in-band-but-outside-your-channel region.
Why it matters: B3 (1710–1880 MHz) is shared by multiple operators — your B3 TX must not pollute an adjacent operator's channel inside the same band. The limit follows the operating-band emission mask (matching ACLR at close offsets).
Multi-band OBUE risk + debug
B1+B3 IM products can land inside the B3 band but outside your channel → OBUE failure even though each carrier alone is clean. Debug: OBUE fail + ACLR pass → inter-band IM, not DPD.
Q: OBUE fails on B3 when B1 active, passes when B1 off — cause? Inter-band IMD: 2×f_B1−f_B3 or 2×f_B3−f_B1 lands inside B3. Not fixable by DPD (it linearises one carrier at a time) — it's a hardware isolation problem between the B1 and B3 PA paths.
FC19 Transmitter Spurious Emissions TX Conformance click to expand +
Why it exists
Spurious emissions (3GPP §6.6.4) are unwanted outputs far from the carrier — harmonics, mixing products, LO leakage — swept from 9 kHz to 12.75 GHz. They must stay under absolute regulatory limits so the PA doesn't pollute other services (and, critically, its own co-located RX band).
Real RCT Implementation — actual code from the test framework
Files: measure_test_lte_Tx_Spurious (conformance_unified_lte_tx_speed.py) → config_te_for_lte_spurious_emissions (utils.py) → sa_load_mask_setup(get_fdd/tdd_spurious_emissions_setup_name) → FETCh:SPURious?.FETCh:SPURious? # per spur: num_spurs, range, idx, freq, ampl, limit, marginKPI (Metro_kpi_thresholds.json → test_lte_Tx_Spurious, [f_start, f_stop, limit_dBm, RBW]):
RangeLimitRBW
9 kHz – 150 kHz−36 dBm1 kHz
150 kHz – 30 MHz−36 dBm10 kHz
30 MHz – 1 GHz−36 dBm100 kHz
1 GHz – 12.75 GHz−30 dBm1 MHz
UL-protection−96 dBm100 kHz
The −96 dBm UL-protection limit is the tight one — it guards the co-located receive band from the TX's own spurs.
Interview Q&A
Q: Why is the −96 dBm UL-protection limit so much tighter than −36 dBm? The RU's own receiver sits right next to the transmitter; a spur landing in the UL band at −36 dBm would desensitize its own RX, so that sub-band is protected to −96 dBm.
Where spurious come from — 5 sources
1. PA harmonics — PA non-linearity makes integer multiples of the carrier. B1 @2140: 2nd 4280, 3rd 6420, 4th 8560 MHz. These move with carrier freq. Suppressed by the duplexer/output filter (need >40 dBc).
2. Clock harmonics — ADC/DAC sample clock (e.g. 245.76 MHz) × N: ×5 = 1228.8, ×9 = 2211.8, ×17 = 4177.9 MHz. These do NOT move with carrier. Suppressed by PCB shielding + ferrite beads.
3. LO leakage — the PLL LO leaks at its own frequency / sub-harmonics, near the carrier offset.
4. PSU switching noise — DC-DC converters (100 kHz–few MHz) couple a comb of low-frequency spurs into the RF path. Fix: ferrites, layout, shielding.
5. Inter-modulation (multi-band) — B1+B3: 2×2140−1842 = 2438 (near B41), 2×1842−2140 = 1544 (B1 UL); higher orders anywhere.
Protected bands — tighter limits
BandFrequencyLimitWhy
GPS L11559–1610 MHz−47 dBmGPS interference
WCDMAoperator-dep.−47 dBmadjacent operator
Public safetyvaries−47 dBmemergency services
A spur at 1575 MHz above −47 dBm = certification FAIL even though it's well under the general −30 dBm limit.

Mode: Basic SA (not LTE mode) · Meas: Spurious Emissions · 9 kHz → 12.75 GHz · Detector: Peak · Sweep: 3–5 min (longest test in RCT).

Debug decision tree
SPUR ABOVE -30 dBm -> change carrier by +5 MHz -> did it move? moved ~10 MHz (2x) -> PA 2nd harmonic -> check duplexer rejection @2f moved ~5 MHz (1x) -> PA fundamental leak / LO product did NOT move -> clock harmonic or PSU switching check clock freq & multiples, DCDC freq, shielding only with 2nd carrier active -> inter-band IMD (hardware isolation; NOT DPD)
Interview Q&A
Q: Spur at 4280 MHz during B1 test, −28 dBm — pass or fail? FAIL: −28 > −30 dBm. Root cause: 2nd harmonic of B1 (2×2140). Check duplexer harmonic rejection at 4280 MHz (want >40 dBc); if OK, check the output filter.
Q: Spur at 1228.8 MHz, carrier B3 1842 MHz — a PA harmonic? No — 1842/1228.8 = 1.5 (not integer). It's 245.76 MHz × 5 = the ADC/DAC clock harmonic. Proof: move carrier to B1 2140 — if the spur stays at 1228.8, it's a clock spur. Fix: clock-distribution shielding, ferrite beads.
Q: All spurious pass single-band, fail with B1+B3 — what problem? Inter-band intermodulation — IM products of B1×B3 appear as spurs. Not a DPD problem (DPD linearises one carrier at a time). Needs a hardware fix: better B1↔B3 PA-path isolation or band-specific filtering after combining.
Worked example — B3 @ 1812.5 MHz / 15 MHz spurious (measured)
The five ranges and what antenna A actually returned:

The 1–12.75 GHz "failures" are analyzer artefacts (next box); the 30 MHz–1 GHz fail is genuinely unexplained (its peak moves per antenna: A 856.6, B 896.1, C 925.7 MHz — a fixed mixer artefact can't move) and is the one place a real 10.8 dB failure might hide — resolved by a 50 Ω termination test.
Why 2nd & 3rd harmonics dominate
A real PA bends near full power; write its curve as a series and feed one tone:Vout = a1*Vin + a2*Vin^2 + a3*Vin^3 + ... cos^2 x -> DC + 2f cos^3 x -> f + 3f => the amplifier MANUFACTURES energy at 2x, 3x... the carrierThree effects kill the higher orders: coefficients collapse (~20 dB/order), the top harmonic gets the smallest share (cos³→¼ at 3f, cos⁵→1⁄16 at 5f), and filters improve with distance — so only the 2nd/3rd realistically threaten the limit. Harmonics worsen with output power; the AAU at 52.5 dBm sits right where curvature matters (same physics as guitar-amp clipping). B1 harmonics: 2× = 3.625, 3× = 5.4375, 4× = 7.25 GHz.
The analyzer-compression artefact — real emission vs measurement artefact
The RU outputs 52.5 dBm; after ~41 dB cable loss +11.5 dBm arrives at the analyzer. A mixer wants −10 to −20 dBm to stay linear — at +11.5 dBm it is 20–30 dB into compression and manufactures its own harmonics of the carrier. Three proofs the 1–12.75 GHz peaks are instrument-born:
1. 5443.3 / 1812.5 = 3.003 (exact 3rd harmonic; B1 gave 4278.7/2140 = 1.999, the 2nd).
2. 1.298187539 GHz is identical across antennas A/B/C to 9 sig-figs — three different cables/branches — so it is generated inside the instrument, not the radio.
3. +13.3 dBm = 39 dBc — too poor for a filtered PA (60–70 dBc), right for a compressed mixer (30–50 dBc).ref_val = pass_criteria_dbm % 10 # conformance_unified_lte_tx_speed.py # Python modulo on negatives: -36 % 10 = +4 , -30 % 10 = 0 # -> analyzer told to expect ~0 dBm while +11.5 dBm arrives -> compressionBench tests to close it: 50 Ω termination (isolates 30 MHz–1 GHz), a 20 dB pad (a real emission drops exactly 20 dB; an artefact collapses further), and fixing the ref-level modulo.
Real RCT gotcha — GRDEV-7734: Spurious could not run on any EXM analyzer
Every TX run aborted with AttributeError: 'KeysightEXM_E6640A' object has no attribute 'sa_set_spur_report_mode_lte_fdd' (utils.py:3657), raised inside test_lte_Tx_Spurious during E-TM 1.1 — which killed the entire test_lte_Tx_sanity item, so Spurious, EVM, Frequency Error and Dynamic Range all produced NO DATA (that's the real reason "dynamic_range had no data" — collateral damage, not a DU/PHY fault).
Root cause: the three spurious SCPI methods live in a shared SpuriousMixin (created 2026-06-25, GRDEV-8244) added to KeysightEXA_N9010B and KeysightPXI_M9410A but missed on KeysightEXM_E6640A. Validated on the E6680A that all the SCPI works (:INST:CONF:LTEAFDD:SPURious, :SENS:SPUR:REPT:MODE MMARgin, :FETCh:SPURious?), so the fix is one line:- class KeysightEXM_E6640A(KeysightEXF_E6550A): + class KeysightEXM_E6640A(SpuriousMixin, KeysightEXF_E6550A):After: EVM and Frequency Error went NO DATA → PASS; the run completes instead of aborting. Never caught because no cadence anywhere executes Spurious (1 of 54 setups run it — ours), so the missing mixin was unreachable dead code. (The EXF E6550A/E6650A classes still have the same gap — left alone, no bench to validate.)
FC20 Per-RFFE IQ Playback (PR 586) — isolate each RFFE × pol RCT Feature click to expand +
Why it exists
Per-RFFE IQ playback (PR 586 / GRDEV-8131) isolates each RF front-end module (RFFE) on each polarisation and measures ACLR/EVM per path, instead of only the combined output. Before this, TX conformance measured the summed signal from all PAs — so if one RFFE/pol was bad you couldn't tell which. Isolation turns off every path but one, so the analyzer sees just that PA. "IQ playback" = the DU replays a pre-generated IQ ETM waveform (deterministic, TX-only) rather than live PHY.
How it works (tx_speed.py:771 → rffe.py)
_run_iq_playback_measurements, gated on iq_playback=True AND rrh.tx_per_rffe_enabled() (rrh[0].RFFE AND rffe_control.tx_per_rffe).per ETM: connect_cli_manager -> telnet localhost:8888 (root/root, '>' prompt) per IQ port (pol A/B/C/D via iq_playback_ant_map): iq_playback {ETM.bin} {port} 0 0 ; wait 5s ; rrh.rffe_restore_all per RFFE 1..N: rffe_isolate(band,rffe,pol): mb-modify-rffe <0/1> band-id: B1=1 B3=3 B8=8 B28=9928 B41=41 (TX not stopped) wait settle_sec (7s) rffe_verify_isolated -> mb-get-pa : only target ENABLED else tag ISOLATION_UNCONFIRMED _iq_measure_one -> measure_test_Tx_* (ACLR/EVM) row tagged RFFE{n}{pol}_ant{k} rffe_restore_all (at end and on failure)
Modes, layout & the two quirks that make it reliable
Two modes: each-RFFE-on-each-pol (per-RFFE isolation) and all-RFFE-on-each-pol (0xf baseline, all PAs). Layout: B1/B3/B41 = "all" (4 RFFE × 4 pol = 16 paths); B8/B28 = "split" (RFFE1,2 → A,B; RFFE3,4 → C,D). Two ECS fixes make it dependable: rffe_restore_all before every measure (else RFFEs stay off → analyzer reads noise, ACLR ≈ 0 / EVM ≈ 90%) and auto-range before ACLR (else the isolated low-power path reads ACLR near the noise floor — see FC01). Run flag: --iq-playback=true. Code: source/products/rrh/mixins/rffe.py (RffeMixin), wired into FHGW.
Interview Q&A
Q: A per-RFFE isolated path reads ACLR 51 dBc but the combined output passes 55 — is the PA bad? Probably not — check the analyzer auto-ranged (sa_set_atten_for_min_clipping). An isolated single-PA path is lower power, so without auto-range ACLR sits near the noise floor; with it you get ~54.5–55.6.
Q: How do you prove only the target RFFE was transmitting? rffe_verify_isolated reads mb-get-pa — if any non-target PA is still ENABLED the row is tagged ISOLATION_UNCONFIRMED, so a bad isolation can't silently pass.
FC11 PA Protection — 3 dB power reduction on carrier activation: how it works and is tested Intermediate click to expand +

PW Internal · pa_protection.py · Cadence P1 (Nightly) — runs once before all other tests

Plain English First
When you activate a carrier, the PA protection state machine should automatically reduce power by ~3 dB to prevent overcurrent. This test verifies that 3 dB reduction actually happens. If it doesn't, the PA could be damaged during carrier activation at full power.
How It Works
Step 1: Read FHGW DAC output current BEFORE carrier activation via rfdc-app --debug
Step 2: Activate carrier
Step 3: Read DAC output current AFTER activation
Step 4: Compute power change magnitude
Pass: change = 3.0 ± 0.2 dB
Pass/Fail
Expected: 3.0 dB reduction Tolerance: ±0.2 dB Range: 2.8–3.2 dB
DAC Map
DAC_MAP in pa_protection.py maps each (fhgw_band, band) pair → (tile_list, block_list)
Missing mapping → RuntimeError at test time with clear message listing known keys
Adding new band = add a row to DAC_MAP
Cadence Behavior
Runs ONCE at the top of test_main_procedure, before the per-group road-trip loop. A PA FAIL does NOT abort remaining tests — returns a verdict dict. Per-band verdicts reported as test_Tx_Pa_Protection_Band_<band>
What If It Fails
No 3 dB reduction detected → PA protection state machine not triggered → check OVERCURRENT register (default must NOT be 0xFF disabled) · Wrong reduction amount → DAC register mismatch → check rfdc.txt personality file · Your unit 509 → B3/B1 overcurrent parameter was 0xFF (disabled by default) — Dileep caught this

FC13 RX Dynamic Range — Receiver Power Sweep Intermediate click to expand +

3GPP §7.3 · test_lte_Rx_DynamicRange1 · Cadence P1 (Nightly)

Plain English First
While TX dynamic range tests how wide a power range the PA can output, RX dynamic range tests whether the receiver can still decode at 95% throughput when the signal sweeps from near-max (−95 dBm) down to near-sensitivity (−108.5 dBm). Tests AGC tracking and ADC linearity across the full input range.
Test Parameters
ParameterValueWhat It Means
range_start−95 dBmStart power — strong signal, easy to decode
range_stop−108.5 dBmEnd power — near sensitivity limit
range_step−1 dBmStep size — sweep downward
min_throughput≥ 95%Must decode at least 95% of blocks at every step
max_BLER≤ 2%Block Error Rate must stay below 2% throughout
Two Variants
DynamicRange1: Dispatcher — auto-selects AWGN or no-AWGN based on hardware license
DynamicRange_AWGN: With AWGN interferer (requires AWGN license on EXM)
DynamicR_no_awgn: Pure power sweep, no interferer
What If It Fails
Fails at high power (−95 dBm) → ADC clipping/saturation → check gain setting · Fails at low power (−108 dBm) → noise floor too high, same as sensitivity failure · Fails mid-range → AGC not tracking → check AGC step register
FC14 RX Blocking & Intermodulation Advanced click to expand +

3GPP §7.5/7.6/7.8 · test_lte_Rx_Blocking / ACS / ICS / Intermodulation · Cadence P2

Plain English First
These tests check if a strong interferer (from a different operator, different band, or adjacent channel) can knock out your reception of a weak wanted signal. Real world: strong 2G tower nearby interfering with your 4G receive.
4 Test Variants
Test3GPPWhat is being blockedInterferer type
test_lte_Rx_ACS7.5Adjacent channel selectivity±BW offset, LTE signal
test_lte_Rx_ICS7.4In-channel selectivity±BW/2 offset — inside channel
test_lte_Rx_NB_blocking7.5Narrow-band blockingSingle CW tone
test_lte_Rx_intermodulation7.8Two interferers mixingCW + LTE at specific offsets
Search Algorithm
Binary search: start_power=−52 dBm → coarse=8 dB → fine=2-3 dB → finest=0.2 dB
BLER threshold: 5%, bler_tolerance: 2-4
fault_power: −15 dBm (safety ceiling to protect LNA)
Test Frequencies
Run at: fb (band bottom), fm (band middle), ft (band top) — 3 frequencies
This catches frequency-dependent filter roll-off at band edges
What If It Fails
ACS fail → LNA IIP3 too low → strong adjacent signal compresses receiver · ICS fail → within-channel spur from LO harmonics · Intermodulation → IM3 product falls in-band → check LNA IIP3 spec · NB blocking → sharp CW tone saturating LNA → check duplexer band rejection
FC15 RSSI — ADC Calibration Accuracy Intermediate click to expand +

PW Internal · test_Rx_RSSI · Cadence P1 (Nightly)

Plain English First
RSSI is how the radio reports signal strength. Two methods exist: CLI gives dBFS (raw ADC level), DU OAM gives dBm (calibrated physical power). This test verifies they agree — and that the ADC calibration (ADC_ADJUST register) is correct. David Bekker's July 1 task: automate this comparison.
Two RSSI Methods
MethodSourceUnitHow
CLI dBFSget_rssi_from_rrh SSH commanddBFS (ADC full-scale ratio)Reads ADC count directly
DU dBmOAM KPI interfacedBm (physical power)Converts using system NF + gain
DSA Formula
sensitivity_limit = base_dbm + DSA(band)
DSA read from: /etc/configs/personalities/<model>-rfdc.txt at test start
ADC mapping: B1 cols A/B/C/D → ADC 0/1/4/5 | B3 cols → ADC 2/3/6/7
Report Columns
RSSI_Ant0, RSSI_Ant1, RSSI_Ant2, RSSI_Ant3 (dBm)
Dbfs_Ant0, Dbfs_Ant1, Dbfs_Ant2, Dbfs_Ant3
DSA[dB] column: DSA value applied per band (appears in all UL conformance sheets)
What If It Fails
CLI and DU differ by >2 dB → ADC_ADJUST register wrong · All antennas wrong → system NF calculation error · One antenna wrong → that ADC path has gain error · RSSI too low → sensitivity is worse than expected (LNA degraded)
Real RCT quirk — B8 RSSI calibration + the TDD iq-playback suffix (ECS)
B8 RSSI cal (rssi_cal[b082028][8]) done the B1-way: run RSSI with offsets = 0, read the raw RSSI per antenna at a known injected power, set offset = injected − raw. Result (validated, all 4 ant within 2 dB): ant1–4 = 41.44 / 41.25 / 40.53 / 39.96. The offset is applied per-antenna as rssi_cal[fhgw_band][band]; without it the RX RSSI test throws KeyError: 'rssi_cal'. (B28's rssi_cal is still 0 — pending B28 cabling.)TDD iq-playback suffix: for TDD bands the iq-playback ETM filename gets a _TDD suffix → ETM{etm}_{bw}MHz_TDD.bin. B41 (TDD) had tried to load the FDD file ETM1_1_10MHz.bin → "Could not open input file". (This is a TX iq-playback fix — full IQ-playback detail is in FC20.)

FWK1 Framework — Architecture & execution (how ruauto runs) Framework click to expand +

ruauto = a pytest framework testing RU/base-station gear (BBU · RRH · CWS) across 2G/3G/4G/5G · docs docs/ARCHITECTURE.md + knowledge_base/test_execution.md

The 3-layer model (strictly enforced)
TEST (source/features/) — the test_*.py cases + assertions. Calls Steps only.
STEPS (source/steps/) — workflows/business logic (CwsSteps, VrpSteps, AttenuatorSteps). Uses Products.
PRODUCT (source/products/) — device drivers (VRU, CWS, NR, HNG, RRH) over SSH/CLI/XML.
⚠ Golden rule: tests never touch a device directly — always through Steps. Products are auto-selected by config (tech + duplex + product flags) via a decorator registry (products/registry.py, @register_product).
Directory → purpose & tech→product map
infrastructure/ core (config, logging, reporting) · features/ suites (tech_2g/tech_4g/{fdd,tdd}/tech_5g) · test_equipment/ instruments · tools/ QXDM/iperf · common/ + TestCase base.
TechProduct classesDuplex
4GVruFdd4g, VruFdd4gFHGW, VruTdd4g, CwsTdd4gFDD & TDD
5GNR_tdd, NR_tdd_Docker, VrpTDD/FDD
2GVruFdd2g, CwsFdd2gFDD
Variants branch on flags fhgw · docker · generic_phy · dual_band · is_4cc · multirat_4g · rct_container.
How a TX run executes (the "road trip")
test_lte_Tx_sanity()      # entry: build test list (CI vs full RCT), config TE
  func()                  # accumulate per-test ETMs/TMs/freqs
  test_lte_Tx_road_trip() # NESTED LOOPS:
    band > BW > power > freq(fb/fm/ft) > ETM > TM > test
      globals()['measure_%s' % test](...)   # dynamic dispatch
Combination math: bands × BWs × powers × freqs × ETMs × TMs × tests — e.g. 3×4×3×3×6×1×5 = ~9,720 measurements. That's why cadence tiers exist (P0 CI is tiny, P2 regression is huge).
Verdicts, fail-rate & retries (source/common/test_case.py)
Verdict values: Pass · Fail · Pass_Tolerance · Not Tested.
update_test_verdict():  fail_count += not_tested_count + fail_count   # ⚠ NOT_TESTED counts as FAIL
write_final_verdict():  fail_rate = fail_count / total * 100   # -> FailRate.txt (Jenkins email)
# retry: up to 2x (restart L1/L2 + retransmit); still no TX -> record NOT_TESTED (= a fail)
Outputs: Excel per-test sheets · Elasticsearch (tc.update_new_elastic, index phy_data-*) · FailRate.txt. Note: an empty verdict list records 1 Fail — so a test that silently produced nothing still counts against you.
FWK2 Framework — KPI thresholds (how pass/fail is resolved) Framework click to expand +

Centralized, 3GPP-traceable limits · doc docs/KPI_THRESHOLDS_README.md · files under kpi_thresholds_references/ (Metro, FHGW_Box, …) selected by setup.ini [kpi_thresholds]

Structure & flavors
Each test entry carries 3gpp_reference, test_parameters, kpi, optional interferer. Limit flavors: frequency-dependent (bands.band_0_3000 / band_3000_4200), bandwidth-dependent (limits."5"/"10"/"15"/"20"), ETM-dependent (etm_limits), band overrides (band_min_limit, key {fhgw_band}_{dualband_step}).
Resolution precedence (highest → lowest)
1. tc_cadence["RRH-Thresholds"]      # per-setup custom RRH override
2. KPI thresholds file               # standard 3GPP values
3. hardcoded default in utils.py     # last-resort fallback
⚠ FHGW inversion gotcha: for FHGW setups, aclr/evm/rx_limits/prach limits were removed from tc_cadence.json and centralized into the KPI JSON — so editing tc_cadence there has no effect. (See it live: Reference Sensitivity's −69 dBm comes from rx_limits_validation_conditions, overriding the 3GPP −101.5.)
FHGW DSA runtime adjustment (GRDEV-6650) — key concept
RX sensitivity/PRACH limits are not fixed in JSON for FHGW. Each RU carries per-ADC DSA (Digital Step Attenuator) values in rfdc.txt. At test start apply_dsa_adjustments_from_ru() SSHes in, reads DSA, and computes:
kpi_limit = base_dbm + DSA(band)     # JSON only stores base_dbm; a DSA[dB] column is logged
Why: each RU/band has different front-end attenuation — one hardcoded sensitivity number would be wrong per unit. So JSON _expected_* / sensitivity_limit values are reference-only and can look "wrong" vs the real pass limit.
Sensitivity search params + validation states
init_power start dBm · coarse_step/fine_step/finest_step search granularity · fault_power abort ceiling · bler_threshold target BLER% · bler_tolerance accept window · bler_100_max_steps abort a dead UL early. Verdict states: min_criteria = strict 3GPP (no tolerance) · pass_criteria = min ± tolerance (measurement uncertainty) · in-between = PASS_TOLERANCE. Validators live in infrastructure/utils.py :: LteUtils. (Doc caveat: KPI_THRESHOLDS_README.md has an unresolved git-stash marker near L122 and lists test_Tx_DLRS twice.)
FWK3 Framework — Troubleshooting (real automation failures & fixes) Framework click to expand +

War-stories from knowledge_base/troubleshooting.md — the kind of thing that eats an afternoon at the bench

Signal-generator / measurement
Ext-delay stuck ~9.9995 ms — for VVDN RUs the code forces ext-delay ON and, missing test_cases[0].ext_delay, falls back to hardcoded 9.9995e-3. Fix: set ext_delay in seconds (e.g. 0.008). (utils.py ~L2208)
MXG error 628 (DAC over range) — ARB runtime scaling too high → DAC clips; output distorted though sg_set_pwr "succeeds". Fix: fix_error_628() steps scaling 80→60→50→30 until clear. (te_equipments.py)
cable_loss missing on KeysightPXI_M9410A — that class needs a leading role arg; instantiating it analyzer-style shifts args so cable_loss looks absent. Fix: pass role; fixture now defaults cable_loss 0 and retries. (pytest_hooks.py)
Test logic / RF
Band-3 blocking wrong CF steps — range-3 in-band interferer used non-uniform steps, missed required 3GPP freqs. Fix: step_of_1MHz=True in get_cf_range_ib_and_oob().
Comba opt8 (LRCP) RX fails at fm/ft, passes fb — LRCP RRUs don't retune a running L1 on carrier change (netopeer ones do); antenna-outer/freq-inner loop left PHY on the old carrier → 100% CRC. Fix (GRDEV-8103): LRCP uses freq-outer _rx_road_trip_lrcp (fresh L1/L2 per freq).
unique_keys empty on CSV merge — RNTI (16-bit MAC) looked up in an IMSI→UE_ID dict (different ID space) → 0 matches. Fix: new ue_identity.py + rnti_ueid_dict → >90% match.
CI / infrastructure
Jenkins SUCCESS but no branch update — MissingPropertyException: SYNC_BRANCH: Groovy interpolates ${SYNC_BRANCH} before bash runs. Fix: escape \$SYNC_BRANCH (or use ''' blocks).
Empty --cadence= — mis-parsed category (e.g. CI ≠ map key ci) makes the lookup return empty. Fix: normalize category, default to P0.
2G opens too many sockets — per-iteration SSH opens (72) but closes only at end (2) → exhaustion. Fix: close L1/L2 SSH after each trx_mode. (vru.py)
FWK4 Framework — S-Plane verification (PTP/SyncE timing) Framework click to expand +

The "S" = Synchronization · features/tech_5g/splane_verification_nr.py · docs SPLANE_AUTOMATION_EXPLANATION.md + knowledge_base/splane_verification.md

Plain English — what & why
In an O-RAN 7.2x split the RU must keep its clock aligned to the network using PTP (IEEE-1588) driven by a Grand Master (GM), backed by GNSS + internal oscillator. Get it wrong → TDD breaks, interference, 3GPP timing fails. Two headline metrics: Frequency Error (Hz / ppb) and Time Alignment Error / TAE (ns). The RU cycles PTP states LOCKED → HOLDOVER → ACQUIRING → LOCKED. Measured by a spectrum analyzer (RF freq/time via EVM table) and a Keysight oscilloscope (physical 1PPS / 10 MHz edge).
The three test types
Holdover — deliberately kill the reference (GNSS or PTP) so the RU free-runs on its oscillator, then measure drift. GM is forced to HOLDOVER before measuring so the whole window is genuine holdover. Variants: GNSS-loss, PTP-loss (C3 topology), two-GM redundancy (4 h scope capture).
Stability — long capture under PTP LOCKED to build statistics (~10 samples/s) + recovery tests (re-lock after PTP restart / full reboot, e.g. "locked in 145.2s").
Temperature monitoring — pre-test that waits for thermal equilibrium first, because oscillators drift with temp (TCXO ~±1 ppm/°C) and would contaminate results.
Config & pre-test flow
GMConfig caches the GM PTP settings (ptp_instance/ptp_port/gnss_port from setup.json "gm"). Cadence hierarchy Cadence-IDs["SPLANE"] → Group-IDs["TS_DL_SPLANE"] → Test-IDs; group carries PreTest[] + Tests[], dispatched via getattr(). Pre-test sequence: wipe FHGW logs → start PTP-packet tcpdump → temperature stabilize → PTP restart → start TX (aborts if all antennas < −20 dBm). PTP-restart polls fetch_lock_state() every 10 s until HOLDOVER, re-enables in a finally, then check_sync_state("LOCKED", timeout=600).
Concrete limits & durations
maxAbsTE < 1100 ns (3GPP, scope — abort on fail) · dTEh < 200 ns (holdover drift rate) · holdover KPIs freq_tolerance 50 ppb, time_offset 300 ns, max_time_error 1500 ns · non-holdover Freq_Error ±185 Hz, TAE 65 ns (±25), EVM 18.5%. Durations: temp stabilize 30 min (±2 °C), holdover/lock timeout 600 s, stability capture 1000 s, scope capture 4 h @ 200 ns/div. Typical "good": ±100 Hz, ±30 ns.

NF1 Noise — Thermal floor kTB = −174 dBm/Hz (the absolute limit) Beginner click to expand▾
PLAIN ENGLISH FIRST Thermal noise in one sentence: Any object above −273°C (absolute zero) has electrons randomly moving around — that random movement creates a tiny electrical noise. In your RU, every resistive component (cable, duplexer, LNA input) generates this noise. The LNA then amplifies it along with the wanted signal. This is why you cannot build a perfectly silent receiver.
Quick link — how this connects to DSA:
Thermal noise (kTB) sets the absolute noise floor. NF1 explains the physics. The full sensitivity formula using kTB + NF + SNR → DSA offset is in the DSA card.
→ For the complete chain (kTB → NF → Sensitivity → DSA → PRACH), open the DSA card.

RCT bench setup — DU, AAU, instruments, connections decoded

Your bench setup — instrument roles:
EXM E6640A: Vector Signal Generator. Injects calibrated UL signals (PRACH preambles at DSA-corrected power levels) into RU BOB SMA for RX/sensitivity tests. Also generates FRC waveforms for RSSI cal.
EXA N9010B: Signal/Spectrum Analyser. Measures TX output: power, ACLR, EVM, spectrum mask. Connect via BOB SMA + 30 dB pad.
VNA E5071C: Network Analyser. Measures S21 (phase) for per-column beamforming calibration, cable loss, connector VSWR.
Connection diagram — RX test (sensitivity/RSSI):
EXM output → SMA cable (measure loss with VNA first) → RU BOB SMA port (UL column under test). EXM controls: frequency = band UL centre, power = target sensitivity + cable_loss, waveform = FRC_A1. RU CLI: get_rssi N to read ADC. DU CLI: testmac rssi to read DU RSSI. All three must agree within ±2 dB.
Connection diagram — TX test (ACLR/power):
RU BOB SMA (DL column under test) → 30 dB attenuator pad → SMA cable → EXA input. EXA: centre freq = band DL centre, atten = 10 dB (+ 30 dB pad = 40 dB total), preamp OFF, ACLR mode. Wait 60s for DPD convergence. Measure: power (compare to rated target ±1 dB), ACLR (compare to −45 dBc limit), EVM if required.

Why thermal noise is unavoidable

Thermal noise and the sensitivity floor:
Any resistive element above 0 K generates thermal noise. In your RX chain: the cable termination, the duplexer, the LNA input — all generate kTB noise. The LNA then amplifies both the incoming signal and all the noise it sees. You cannot eliminate this noise — you can only minimise the noise added after the signal enters the chain (which is what good LNA design does). This is why cryogenic receivers used in radio astronomy cool the LNA to near 0 K — it is the only way to get below the room-temperature kTB floor.
Noise voltage — how it appears on a spectrum analyser:
Noise voltage Vn = √(4kTBR). For a 50Ω system at 290K in 1MHz bandwidth: Vn = √(4 × 1.38e-23 × 290 × 1e6 × 50) = 0.895 μV = −107 dBm. On your EXA with preamp ON, this appears as the noise floor — the flat baseline across the span. When you inject a signal that rises above this floor, you can measure it. When the signal drops below it, it is lost in the noise.
📐 Real numbers — how temperature changes thermal noise

T = 233K
kTB = −175.6 dBm/Hz

T = 290K (reference)
kTB = −174 dBm/Hz
